title: Step 1: The simple model

design.question: On a generated idea graph, how far does a society get for the same money, by α and β?
design.fixed: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7), 12 identical agents, budget 1200 split equally, no flat mint, knowledge reward 1 per new bit, no validation
design.measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste

answer: Best overall: OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste. (8 measures; a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)
answers: hardest level: 6.00 against traditional 0.24, clearly better.
targets solved: 2.00 against traditional 0.05, clearly better.
bounty value: 256 against traditional 6.40, clearly better.
knowledge found (bits): 101 against traditional 60, clearly better.
knowledge per unit of money: 0.25 against traditional 0.05, clearly better.
money to the main level: 283 against traditional 1104, clearly better.
caveats: A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
